solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Something staged disturbed comrades of yore? About right

indicators.note: About means going round, so the rearranged letters surround the abbreviation for right
disturbed letters are knocked out of their order, so the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned question about comrades of long ago being upset, with an afterthought about being on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' shuffles the old comrades, and 'About' wraps that shuffle round the letter for right; the staged something is Shakespeare's play.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's farce of mistaken twins is a play, something put on a stage.

clue.text: A stick put up containing fit electrical item

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so the reversed stick wraps round the word for fit
put up in a down clue means raised, so the stick is read bottom to top

parts.note: a rod is a stick
apt means fit or suitable

explanation.surface: A stick raised up holds a suitable electrical gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns ROD into DOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An adaptor is an electrical fitting connecting plugs and sockets of different types.

clue.text: Musician ranks matter to entertain ambassador

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the matter holds the ambassador inside

parts.note: pus is the matter in an infected wound
HE is His Excellency, the form of address for an ambassador

explanation.surface: Ordinary soldiers have business entertaining a diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'matter' looks like a verb or subject; it is pus.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this lyre player charmed beasts and descended to the underworld with his music.

clue.text: Two teens when tipsy consuming drink that's compact

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing, so the jumbled letters take in the drink
when tipsy the letters stagger about into a new order

parts.note: two teens are two copies of the word teen side by side
a cordial is a sweet drink

explanation.surface: A couple of teenagers, tipsy, drinking - a compact one's handbag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when tipsy' shuffles the pair of teens and 'consuming' sets the drink inside; 'compact' is not a powder case but a treaty.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1904 Anglo-French agreement, an understanding or pact between nations.

clue.text: Having toured India, most eye wild park

indicators.note: having toured means going all round, so the scrambled letters surround the letter for India
wild means unruly, so the letters of most and eye are mixed up

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: After a trip round India, most eyes are on a park with wild scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Yosemite is a famous national park in California's Sierra Nevada.

clue.text: Stronghold keeping fashionable tin from Budapest?

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the stronghold holds the word for fashionable

parts.note: a fort is a stronghold
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A fortress storing trendy tin, perhaps from Hungary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tin' is slang for money, not the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: The forint is Hungary's currency, so it is money from its capital.

clue.text: Manage a mood with character heading off and feel unwell?

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
a temper is a mood

indicators.note: heading off means its first letter is removed

parts.note: nature is character

explanation.surface: Coping with a bad mood and a personality off at a tangent - and feeling ill?
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' drops N from NATURE, leaving ATURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a fever, the body's heat raised above normal, is how one feels unwell.

clue.text: Timeless Italian football team and company in river

indicators.note: timeless means without T, the abbreviation for time

parts.note: Torino is a football club from Turin

explanation.surface: An Italian football club and its firm are in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Timeless' drops T from TORINO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orinoco is a major South American river flowing through Venezuela.

clue.text: Authority once on board to get through test held by TV station

indicators.note: held by means inside, so the word for succeeding in an exam goes within the TV channel

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite television broadcaster
to pass is to get through an exam

explanation.surface: A former official on a committee must pass a test run by a broadcaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' means at the chessboard: Boris Spassky was world chess champion 1969-72.
explanation.definitionFit: A former world chess champion is an old authority at the board game.

clue.text: Wild praise about favourite course for beginners?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the synonym for favourite
wild suggests something out of control, so the letters of praise are jumbled

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Effusive commendation about a favourite introductory course for novices.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'beginners': not novices but the start of a meal, a starter course.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter dish opens a meal, a course for those just beginning to eat.

clue.text: Note appearance made by a Nigerian currency

parts.note: an air is an appearance or manner, as in an air of confidence

explanation.surface: A banknote's look is created by a Nigerian currency.
explanation.definitionFit: The monetary unit of Nigeria, divided into a hundred kobo.

clue.text: Asian reportedly favoured book in promotion?

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken, so the word for a person from Thailand is taken by its sound

parts.note: a Thai is an Asian person from Thailand
in means popular or favoured, as in the in crowd

explanation.surface: An Asian person apparently preferred a book in a sales campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is a book published alongside a film or TV series to promote and profit from it.

clue.text: Horrible battle site tours devised

parts.note: Mons in Belgium was the site of a famous 1914 battle

indicators.note: devised means worked out or made up, so the letters of tours are newly arranged

explanation.surface: Tours of a battlefield, ghoulishly planned, are dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: MONS was the first British battle of the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something shocking, hideous or outrageous.

clue.text: Poet and explorer with unusual title left out

parts.note: James Clark Ross was a polar explorer

indicators.note: unusual signals the remaining letters of title are put into an odd order
out says one letter is dropped from title before rearranging

explanation.surface: A poet and an explorer, with an odd title omitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out' drops L from TITLE; 'unusual' rearranges the remaining TITE as ETTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Christina and Dante Gabriel Rossetti were both Victorian poets.

clue.text: Express outward signs of dismay after English mob rampaged

indicators.note: after places the outer letters of dismay behind the earlier parts
a mob that rampaged ran wild, so its letters are thrown about
outward signs of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Showing alarm after an English crowd ran riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rampaged' turns MOB into MBO.
explanation.definitionFit: To express a quality is to give it concrete form, to personify or represent it.

clue.text: Dictatorial type in US car, loveless Eastern European

parts.note: auto is American for car

indicators.note: loveless means without O, which is love or zero in tennis

parts.note: a Croat is someone from Croatia

explanation.surface: A despot in an American car, an Eastern European with no love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' drops the O from CROAT.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocrat is a ruler holding absolute power, a dictator.

clue.text: Some hero's to visit Russian port

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A hero is to visit a Russian seaport.
explanation.definitionFit: Rostov-on-Don is a river port in southern Russia near the Sea of Azov.

clue.text: Fishy dish with some bread Englishman held up

parts.note: a roll is a small loaf of bread

indicators.note: held up in a down clue means raised, so the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: Pom is Australian slang for an English person

explanation.surface: An Englishman holds up a fish dish and some bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held up' turns POM into MOP.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollmop is a pickled herring fillet rolled around onion, a fish dish.

clue.text: Plans run possibly avoiding the latest evidence of congestion?

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged otherwise
avoiding the latest means the final letter of the word run is left out

explanation.surface: Plans perhaps run without the newest evidence of traffic jams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding the latest' cuts RUN to RU; 'possibly' rearranges PLANSRU.
explanation.definitionFit: A snarl-up is a traffic jam, the tangle that shows roads are clogged.

clue.text: Long period after fuel's spilt in body of plane

indicators.note: after puts the long period behind the scrambled letters
spilt fuel is scattered, so its letters are scrambled

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Fuel has been leaking into an aircraft for a long time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilt' turns FUELS into FUSEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuselage is the main body of an aircraft, carrying crew and passengers.

clue.text: A learner queried role taking in good lively piece

parts.note: L is the learner plate symbol

indicators.note: taking in means holding inside, so the reshuffled letters take in the letter for good
queried means questioned, so the letters of role are put in doubt and reshuffled

explanation.surface: A learner questioned a part that includes a good lively piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'queried' turns ROLE into LERO.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is a musical direction meaning fast and lively, also a movement played so.

clue.text: Passage from back of counter in bar

indicators.note: in places the final letter inside the word for bar

parts.note: bar means except, as in all bar one

indicators.note: back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: Getting from behind a pub counter into the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub; it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: An excerpt is a passage taken from a longer text or piece.

clue.text: Poems with appeal in foreign port

parts.note: odes are lyric poems
SA is sex appeal

explanation.surface: Poems with charm set in a port abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Odessa is a major Black Sea port in Ukraine.

clue.text: Resort and country bordering lake sound possibly but lacking sun

indicators.note: bordering puts the country right next to the lake

parts.note: land is a country, as in a foreign land

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of sound may be rearranged
lacking says a letter is dropped from sound before reordering

explanation.surface: A holiday spot beside a lake that might have a sound, though no sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking sun' takes S from SOUND; 'possibly' rearranges OUND as UDNO.
explanation.definitionFit: Llandudno is a Victorian seaside resort town on the North Wales coast.

clue.text: First signs of ancient university looming in cloisters — like a court?

indicators.note: first signs of words are their opening letters, taken in order

explanation.surface: An ancient university looms through its cloisters, with a stately, courtly air.
explanation.definitionFit: Aulic means relating to a royal court, from Latin aula, a hall.

clue.text: Feature of church mostly seen after mass in island

indicators.note: seen after puts the shortened church feature behind the abbreviation for mass

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: the altar is the table at the east end of a church

explanation.surface: A church's furnishing, mostly visible after Mass, on a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' tempts as the church service; here it is M.
explanation.definitionFit: Malta is a Mediterranean island nation south of Sicily.

clue.text: An appealing sponge?

parts.note: sponge here is a person who lives off others, and appealing means making requests, not attractive

explanation.surface: An attractive bath sponge.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadger lives off others by begging, a parasitic person forever asking for handouts.

clue.text: Overcome at the last minute — like angry sentry on duty?

definitions.meaning: beaten narrowly right at the finish of a race
pipped means annoyed, and a sentry on duty stands at his post

explanation.surface: Beaten at the death, like a furious guard standing at his station.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means narrowly beaten at the finishing line, the post ending a race.
